Senses.Explanation: The term credits or tests demonstrated competence: an adept, a real hand. Yuanwu Keqin applies it to an interlocutor who handles an exchange, to an adept lineage teacher who frees people from entanglement, to a meeting conducted on adept terms, and to an adept Chan guest who acts as soon as a case is raised. Pang Yun exclaims it as direct praise. Xinghua Cunjiang compounds it with battle-general and demands a direct advance. Qingping Weikuang dismisses the approaching participant as not an adept. In a poetic exchange an unnamed interlocutor uses it with poet, showing that the competence belongs to the role supplied by context rather than defining only a Chan office. The corpus supports expert status, not the modern default sense author or writer. Independent later witnesses apply it to the means required of a teaching-seat master and even to Emperor Zhuangzong as an ‘adept ruler’; the competence follows the supplied role. A corpus-wide control for the ordinary verbs ‘compose,’ ‘write,’ and ‘compile,’ the ordinary noun ‘author,’ and the compound ‘adept poet’ found author/composer grammar named by other words, while the headword continues to predicate demonstrated capability.
Senses.Note: Ten exact witnesses across six distinct works. Occupational/author controls were actively tested; no curated line requires modern ‘author/writer’ as the bare-headword referent.
